# Catalogues

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-catalogues-doc from
     hypergumbo_core.yaml_catalogs; edit catalogues_doc.py, not this file. -->

hypergumbo's analyses run on **catalogues**: YAML rows that say which calls
are I/O, which values are tainted, what makes them safe, what a library
returns, how a framework dispatches. This page says whose word each row is,
what that lets it do to a verdict, and how to add your own
([ADR-0061](adr/0061-catalogue-tiers-for-every-family.md)).

## The four tiers

| tier | what | vouched for by | where it lives | can it make a verdict cleaner? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **built-in** | standard-library and platform rows | hypergumbo | the installed package, `provenance: builtin` | yes |
| **community** | third-party library rows, shipped but not maintained, dated by `retrieved:` | nobody | the installed package, `provenance: community` | no: it can add a finding, never remove one or an uncertainty |
| **yours** | rows you supply | you | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hypergumbo/` (`config.toml`, one `<family>.d/` per family below), or a file you name on the command line | yes, and a clean verdict that relied on your sanitizer or terminating summary says so (exit 3) |
| **in-repo** | catalogue data inside the analysed repository that you did not name | nobody, until you opt in | the catalogue keys of `<repo>/.hypergumbo.toml` | only after you opt in |

A row makes a verdict *cleaner* when it can move it toward `confirmed`: a
sanitizer, a summary that ends a taint branch, a `module_completeness` grant,
an I/O row that makes a call count as examined, a library signature that
types a receiver. A source, a sink, a framework pattern or an I/O detection
only ever adds.

**What a community row may not do, exactly.** A community I/O row never makes
a call count as examined, and its `module_completeness` grants are withheld; a
community taint sanitizer is not a barrier (the flow is reported and names it,
`withheld_community_sanitizer`); a community terminating summary never closes
a taint branch (`withheld_community_summary`). Community `frameworks`,
`dataflow_patterns` and `library_signatures` rows are disclosed rather than
withheld: measured with every one of them removed, they made no verdict
cleaner, only added structure and flows (ADR-0061 ruling 2).

**A file's tier is its own `provenance:` line**, never the directory it sits
in. A community file you copy into your config home is still community;
deleting its `provenance: community` line is how you vouch for it, and it is
then yours.

## Every family

| family | built-in files | community files | your channel | what it is for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `frameworks` | 8 | 99 | `frameworks.d/` | Without these, a symbol is just a function: decorators, annotations and naming conventions stop being read as routes, handlers or entrypoints, so reachability starts from less than it should. |
| `dataflow_patterns` | 20 | 1 | `dataflow_patterns.d/`, `library_patterns` only | Decides whether a call READS or MUTATES its receiver. Without them the taint walk cannot tell `x.append(secret)` from `len(x)`. |
| `io_primitives` | 15 | 0 | `io_primitives.d/` | The rows that make a call count as I/O at all. Without them no boundary is recognised, every boundary claim goes inconclusive, and a repository looks clean because nothing was examined. |
| `io_primitives_overlays` | 0 | 8 | none | Third-party I/O that hypergumbo ships but does NOT vouch for. Without them a call to `requests.post` is invisible, because hypergumbo analyses your repository and not site-packages. |
| `cfg_nodes` | 6 | 0 | none | Maps tree-sitter node types to control flow. Without them the CFG for that language is empty, and an empty CFG silently means an empty taint walk. |
| `taint_sources` | 2 | 2 | `taint_sources.d/` | Declares which values arrive untrusted. Without them a flow has no beginning and nothing is reported, however far the value travels. |
| `taint_sanitizers` | 1 | 1 | `taint_sanitizers.d/` | Declares what makes a tainted value safe. Without them real flows stay reported after they have been made harmless — noise, not risk. |
| `taint_sinks` | 2 | 0 | `taint_sinks.d/` | Declares the sinks no I/O boundary can derive — evaluating data as code, writing it into a page as HTML. Without them a claim cannot forbid code or DOM injection at all (ADR-0060). |
| `function_summaries` | 4 | 3 | `function_summaries.d/`, rides the user-supplied caveat | Describes callees whose source is not analysed. A wrong 'terminates' verdict closes a branch that is really open and DELETES a real finding, which is why a user-supplied one rides a caveat. |
| `url_folding` | 2 | 0 | none | Folds a built URL back to a route pattern. Without them an interpolated URL never matches the route it calls. |
| `library_signatures` | 5 | 2 | `library_signatures.d/` | Says what a LIBRARY function returns, which is the only way a receiver bound to a library call can be typed at all — nothing in your repository declares it. Without them such a receiver stays on the `external` sentinel and every method-kind row keyed by its type is unreachable however correct that row is. |

Families with no channel say why in the registry: their rows describe grammar node types or hypergumbo's own engines (`cfg_nodes`, `url_folding`), or they have a home already (`io_primitives_overlays` rows are overridden from `io_primitives.d/`).

## Adding your own rows

Drop a YAML file in the family's channel under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hypergumbo/`. A minimal row for each:

### `frameworks.d/` (frameworks)

```yaml
# frameworks.d/<framework id>.yaml REPLACES the shipped definition of
# that framework whole (a definition is one coherent convention).
id: inhouse_web
language: python
patterns:
  - concept: route
    decorator: "^app\\.route$"
    extract_path: "args[0]"
```

### `dataflow_patterns.d/` (dataflow_patterns)

```yaml
# dataflow_patterns.d/<language>.yaml -- only library_patterns is read
language: python
library_patterns:
  - match: '\.enqueue\('
    access_mode: write
```

### `io_primitives.d/` (io_primitives)

```yaml
language: python
status: overlay
retrieved: 2026-09-30        # when you last checked the library
net_send:
  - module: inhouse_http
    functions: [post]
```

### `taint_sources.d/` (taint_sources)

```yaml
taint_label: pii
sources:
  python:
    - module: crm
      functions: [lookup]
```

### `taint_sanitizers.d/` (taint_sanitizers)

```yaml
transforms:
  - input_taint: pii
    output_taint: redacted
    functions:
      python:
        - crm.redact       # rides the user-supplied-sanitizer caveat
```

### `taint_sinks.d/` (taint_sinks)

```yaml
zone: audit_log
trust_level: untrusted
sinks:
  python:
    - module: audit
      functions: [record]
```

### `function_summaries.d/` (function_summaries)

```yaml
summaries:
  - function: "inhouse_log.record"
    param_to_return: {}
    side_effect: true      # TERMINATING: rides the user-supplied caveat
```

### `library_signatures.d/` (library_signatures)

```yaml
# library_signatures.d/<language>.yaml
language: go
signatures:
  inhouse.Open: inhouse.Handle
```

## Opting in to a repository's own catalogue data

A repository's `.hypergumbo.toml` may set preferences (`[merge]`, `[backends]`),
and those load by default. Its **catalogue** keys (today `io_primitives`) load
only when you opt in:

- for one run: `--in-repo-catalogues` (`io-boundaries`, `verify-claims`);
- for one repository: `hypergumbo trust-catalogues [PATH]`, recorded under
  `$XDG_STATE_HOME/hypergumbo/` and keyed by the resolved path
  (`--revoke` records a refusal, `--show` prints the decision).

A file you name on the command line (`--claims`, `--io-primitives`,
`--taint-*`) is opted in by naming it. Until you decide, a run that skips
in-repo catalogue data says which files it did not load.

## Turning community rows off

`--no-default-overlays` omits community rows from the verify step: the
shipped community I/O overlays, every overlay declaring
`provenance: community`, the taint sinks and sources derived from them, and
the community taint and function-summary files. It does not reach the
analysis that builds the graph.

## Seeing what a run rested on

- `verify-claims --format json` lists every catalogue file the run read under
  `catalog_provenance.tiers` (`builtin` / `community` / `yours` / `in_repo`,
  with git state `committed` / `modified` / `untracked` for a file inside the
  repository), names every `module_completeness` grant and where it came from,
  and lists a community file's withheld grants separately.
- `hypergumbo catalog-inventory` shows each family, its file count, your
  channel and whether it is read.
- `hypergumbo init-catalogs` creates your catalogue home and seeds the
  community I/O overlays into `io_primitives.d/` so you can edit them.
